skill.name: security-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze project security posture with dependency, container, cloud, and secret exposure discovery. Query OSV.dev and generate technical and executive remediation reports.
skill.summary: Scan project assets, check OSV.dev vulnerabilities, and draft prioritized security remediation reports.
skill.author: Cornjebus

security_audit.summary: AI review found that the high static score is driven by expected security scanner behavior and Markdown or generated-code examples. The scripts query OSV.dev for dependency vulnerabilities, enumerate .env filenames without reading values, and generate reports instead of executing fixes. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden command execution evidence was found.

remediation.issue: OSV.dev lookups disclose package metadata to an external service.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact data sent to OSV.dev and ask users to confirm scans for private projects.

remediation.issue: Environment file discovery records full local paths in inventory output.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer relative paths for .env findings and keep the existing rule to avoid reading or printing secret values.

remediation.issue: Generated fix commands are displayed as shell guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Label commands as review-before-run and validate package names and versions before presenting shell commands.

content.value_statement: Security reviews are slow when dependency, container, and IaC data are spread across a repository. This skill inventories assets, checks OSV.dev, and drafts prioritized remediation reports.
actual_capabilities: Discovers npm, pip, gem, and Go dependencies from common manifest files.
Finds Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Terraform, and CloudFormation configuration files.
Flags .env style files that may be exposed without reading secret values.
Queries OSV.dev for known open source dependency vulnerabilities.
Calculates simple vulnerability risk scores from severity, exploitability, criticality, and exposure.
Generates technical and executive security report content with remediation guidance.
limitations: OSV.dev lookups send package names and versions to an external service.
The scanner does not replace manual penetration testing or threat modeling.
Generated fix commands and validation tests require human review before use.
Coverage depends on supported manifest and infrastructure file patterns.

use_cases.title: Repository Security Review
use_cases.description: Inventory dependencies, containers, infrastructure files, and possible secret exposure before a release.

use_cases.title: DevOps Configuration Check
use_cases.description: Identify container and cloud configuration files that need security review and remediation planning.

use_cases.title: Remediation Planning
use_cases.description: Turn vulnerability scan results into prioritized technical and executive report sections.

prompt_templates.title: Scan a Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of the current repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use security-analyzer to scan this repository and summarize dependency, container, IaC, and secret exposure risks.

prompt_templates.title: Review Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Use security-analyzer to inventory supported dependency manifests, query OSV.dev, and rank findings by remediation priority.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Remediation
prompt_templates.scenario: Create an engineering remediation plan from scan results.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use security-analyzer to create a phased remediation plan with risk scores, owner-ready actions, and validation test guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Leadership Report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use security-analyzer to produce an executive summary and a technical report from the latest inventory and vulnerability results.

output_examples.input: Run a security scan before release.
output_examples.output: The skill reports dependency counts, container and IaC files, secret exposure risk, OSV.dev vulnerability totals, and priority phases.

output_examples.input: Explain the highest risk dependency issues.
output_examples.output: The skill lists top vulnerabilities with affected packages, severity, risk score, remediation direction, and validation guidance.
The skill summarizes overall posture, vulnerability counts by priority, estimated remediation effort, and recommended next actions.

best_practices: Run scans from the intended project root and review the inventory before sharing results.
Confirm external OSV.dev lookups are acceptable for private package names and versions.
Review generated fix commands and tests before applying changes to production projects.
anti_patterns: Do not run scans on repositories that contain secrets unless handling rules are clear.
Do not execute generated remediation commands without validating package names and versions.
Do not treat generated reports as a complete security assessment without human review.

faq.question: Does this skill read secret values?
faq.answer: The included discovery script flags .env style filenames and gitignore exposure. It is designed not to read secret values.

faq.question: Does it use external network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The vulnerability scanner queries OSV.dev with package names, versions, and ecosystem names.

faq.question: Can it scan containers and cloud files?
faq.answer: It can find Docker, Docker Compose, Kubernetes, Terraform, and CloudFormation files for review context.

faq.question: Does it automatically fix vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It generates remediation guidance, report content, and validation test ideas for review.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I verify before publishing reports?
faq.answer: Verify package names, vulnerability details, risk scores, generated commands, and any external data sharing requirements.
